en.html:
Kageaki(............)
Kanae(Some foolishness is being prepared in there, no?)
Kageaki(...There should at least be parachutes somewhere aboard. Captain, if you would leave this place to me—)
Kanae(And the time for this parachute hunt is available where?)
Kageaki(But...)
Kanae(No but. Keep it.)
Kageaki(...Even so, Captain. My advice brought about this attempt. Answering for the consequences should therefore be my single-person duty.)
Kanae(You told me what you thought Yamato’s future should be, Kageaki. I heard you. I decided to do this. That last part was not done by somebody else.)
Kanae(This duty of yours to carry everything alone—where have you manufactured it from?)
Kageaki(...But—)
Kanae(But is prohibited. Second notice.)
Kageaki(............And... you are content with that?)
Kanae(It is not a matter of good or bad. I am an Ootori.)
Kanae(For this country, what must be done, I do. That is my duty. My blood gives that order.)
Kageaki(...)

en.html:
Captain Ootori answered his weary muttering with banter.
...No. Not banter merely. Time-buying work.

Pull him into conversation, keep his mouth occupied. That was the intention.

But this was not the straight-line officer now standing behind him. Cannon was another account entirely. Would this trick work on him...?

en.html:
Cannon"Hmm? Haan, fair enough. Let us see what surprise is in stock."
Cannon"What brings the three of you aboard?"
Kanae"A morning walk. It occurred to me that taking it in the sky for a change would be rather pleasant."
Cannon"Morning exercise, very healthy. Enjoyment, however, must have been in short supply?"
Kanae"You are planning to improve on that shortly, are you not, Lieutenant Colonel?"
Cannon"What would you mean by that?"
Kanae"A fireworks display, I hear? A little bird brought me the news."
Cannon"...A little bird, is it. Oye, George. Watching from heaven? Since you went and died on Enoshima, this is our section’s information security. Full bird sanctuary."
Kageaki"..."
Cannon"Fireworks. Yes, we do have one large specimen to drop."
Cannon"Wanting to watch, you should have booked first. Guests are guests; I would like to provide the best seats. But arriving suddenly like this—how to arrange?"
Cannon"A gentleman neglecting his guests. My good name will be left standing in its underwear."
Kanae"The bad manners are ours. Please leave your good name in peace. Besides, we have not come to watch."
Cannon"Oh? Some other purpose?"

キャノン「お三方、ご来船の目的は？」
香奈枝「朝の散歩に。 　たまには空でというのも一興かと思い立ち まして」
キャノン「それは健康的なことだ。 　しかし、大して面白くもなかったろう？」
香奈枝「これから面白くする予定ではありませんの？ 　中佐」
キャノン「どういうことかな」
香奈枝「花火大会をなさるんでしょう？ 　風の噂で耳にしましてよ」
キャノン「……風の噂・・・、か。 　ヘイジョージ、天国から見てるか？　お前 さんが江ノ島でくたばっちまって以来、うち の課の情報管理はこんなザマだよ」
景明「……」
キャノン「花火ね。 　確かにでかいやつを一つ、打ち落とす・・・予定 だが」
キャノン「見たいなら事前に申し込んで欲しかったな。 　せっかくの客だ、こっちだって最高の席を 用意して差し上げたいが……急に来られちゃ そうもいかない」
キャノン「客人に礼を欠くのは紳士の恥ってものだ」
香奈枝「非礼はこちら。どうかお気になさらず。 　それにわたくしどもは、見物に参ったわけ ではありませんし」
キャノン「ほう？ 　他に何か目的が？」

Cannon"Arre, have some mercy! You do that, and these perfectly good fireworks become completely useless!"
Kanae"And if that is precisely what I intend?"
Cannon"Hai, what a betrayal. I was thinking, here is one understanding person..."
Kanae"Yes. At least, I was not completely opposed. Only, my mind has since changed."
Cannon"In what direction?"
Kanae"John Bull, ghar jao. Go home☆"
Cannon"...Expelling the foreigners is hardly the fashion."
Kanae"A visitor coming to visit, one can welcome. When he walks in with dirty boots and starts changing the nameplate also—how long is the hostess expected to go on smiling?"
Cannon"But this decision is not entirely your own, noble lady? Somebody has egged you on."
Cannon"That fellow there? The smile-stealing scoundrel?"
Kanae"Correct deduction, filthy wording. Egged me on! Kageaki and I are joined by true love!"
Cannon"Women being deceived always say the same thing."
Sayo"They do indeed."
Kageaki"That is true."
Shipboard Dragoon"Yes."
Kanae"ACHHA!? On THIS point suddenly everybody is united!?"

香奈枝「そうしたいんだと申し上げたら？」
キャノン「なんてこった。 　君は理解者だと信じていたんだがな……」
香奈枝「そうですね。少なくとも完全な反対はして おりませんでした。 　けれど、考えが変わってしまいましたの」
キャノン「どんな風にだい？」
香奈枝「帰れ英国紳士ジョンブル・ゴー・ホーム☆」
キャノン「……攘夷主義エクスクリュージョニズムなんて流行らないぞ」
香奈枝「来るだけなら歓迎もできますけれどね。 　土足で踏み込んだ挙句に表札まで書き換え るつもりのお客さんには、笑顔を向けるのも 限度がございましてよ」
キャノン「しかしそれはあなた一人の決意ではないな、 貴婦人レディ？ 　誰かに唆そそのかされたんだろう」
キャノン「そこの彼かな？ 　君の笑顔を俺から奪った憎い奴は」
香奈枝「ご明察。でも唆したなんて人聞きの悪い。 　わたくしと景明さまは真実の愛で結ばれて おりますのよ！」
キャノン「騙される女はいつも同じことを言う」
さよ「そうですねぇ」
景明「確かに」
船内竜兵「うん」
香奈枝「なんでこんなところでそろって同意!?」

en.html:
The occupation lieutenant colonel shrugged.

Why?

Why was he letting us buy time?
Not even... showing suspicion.

We wanted to stop the bomb being dropped. For us, more time meant victory. He wanted to drop it. His requirement should have been the opposite: less time.
Get the bomb back immediately. That was his job.

And yet.


...Ulta. Turn the conditions around, and the contradiction disappeared.

Not us.
He was the one who needed to buy time. That was the whole thing.

Which meant—

ja.html:
進駐軍中佐が肩をすくめる。

　何故。

　何故、彼はこちらに時間を<ruby>稼がせる<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>？
　何も……疑念を示さずに。

　爆弾を投下させたくないこちらにとって時間を稼ぐ
事が勝利条件ならば、爆弾を投下したい彼の勝利条件
は時間を切り詰める事。
　即刻に爆弾を取り戻さねばならない筈だ。

　だというのに。


　……この矛盾を解く鍵は、勝利条件の逆転にある。

　時間を稼ぐ必要があったのは、こちらではなかった。
　<ruby>彼だった<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>。そういう事だ。

　つまり。
